explanation: Compared against OEIS A253187: a(n) = number of ways to write n as a pentagonal number x(3x−1)/2, plus a second pentagonal number y(3y+1)/2 (x, y ≥ 0), plus a generalized decagonal number m(4m−3) (m ∈ ℤ); Sun conjectures a(n) > 0. In `a`, polygonalNumber 5 x = x(3x−1)/2 and generalizedPolygonalNumber 5 (−y) = y(3y+1)/2. The decagonal test 16r+9 = square is exactly r = m(4m−3), since (8m−3)² = 16r+9, and the integer m is unique because s odd means only one of (3±s)/8 is an integer. So it contributes 1 per representation. The ranges up to n suffice, and the values a(0..4) = 1,2,2,2,1 match the data. Faithful.
